n: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary
s: Asmara calls it 'the Cathedral' -- it never quite was
w: Built in 1923 in Lombard Romanesque style to serve Italian Eritrea's Catholic vicariate, this church has been called 'the Cathedral' since the day it opened -- and never technically was one, since its vicariate never got a bishop's seat. Everyone still calls it that.
_facts: Catholic church built in the early 1920s (1923) in Asmara, Lombard Romanesque style
often called 'The Cathedral' though never the seat of a diocesan bishop, only an apostolic vicariate
principal church of the Apostolic Vicariate of Eritrea

s: The last trace of Eritrea's vanished Jewish community
w: Completed in 1906, this Orthodox synagogue is the only surviving remnant of a Jewish community that once lived alongside colonial Asmara's Italians and Eritreans. Everyone else who worshipped here has long since gone; the building never did.
_facts: Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue in Asmara, Eritrea
the only surviving remnant of the Jewish community in Eritrea

s: Asmara's 1918 opera house, still the city's stage
w: Odoardo Cavagnari designed this theatre-opera house in 1918, one of the first grand stages to rise in what would become Africa's Art Deco capital. Renovated in the 1930s, it still stands where Italian Eritrea first learned to sit through an overture.
_facts: theatre in Asmara, Eritrea, also known as Asmara Opera
constructed in 1918, designed by Italian engineer Odoardo Cavagnari
